published_prior_art.cite: DattaStein2026 gives consistency from local differences/Laplacians, and KeshavarzNguyenScott2019 gives scalar covariance-parameter asymptotics, not this actual-design bivariate ratio-moment Gaussian experiment.

DattaStein2026 establishes estimability and consistent local estimators, while AndrewsMikusheva2016 supplies generic weak-identification calibration; neither proves uniform spatial confidence-set diameter and risk through a disappearing cross-tail exponent.
Li2022 concerns scalar Matérn microergodic inference and CaiLow2004 gives abstract honest-interval tools, not the complete observed bivariate slope experiment with signed cross-tail nuisance.
AndrewsMikusheva2016 supplies conditional weak-identification methods but not attainable Gaussian-tube calibration for this changing spatial cone and its endpoint/tangent limits.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes consistent infill estimability of the slope and gives local-difference/Laplacian-based consistent estimators; the inspected theorem text does not state the proposal's uniform root-N confidence-set, expected-diameter, or risk result.

The paper ties high-frequency unconfoundedness in its common-range Matérn specification to cross-smoothness exceeding exposure smoothness and gives sufficient identifiability conditions for remaining parameters; it does not supply the proposed fixed-domain uniform inference experiment.

source_verification_receipts.version: author manuscript corresponding to Electronic Journal of Statistics 13(2), 4224-4279
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The results establish root-n consistency and asymptotic normality for the local inversion-free covariance estimator in irregular-lattice Matérn settings, rather than a joint bivariate slope-profile experiment.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 105(491), 1167-1177
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article specifies bivariate Matérn marginal and cross-covariance parameters and gives sufficient validity conditions, consistent with using a separately imposed spectral positive-definiteness margin in the proposed subclass.
